title: Fix music playback audio not playing in Mood Music UI

requirements.summary: Debug and fix the audio playback issue so that clicking play on a track plays sound audibly through device speakers/headphones
acceptanceCriteria: When the user selects a mood and clicks the play button on any track in the TrackList, audio plays audibly
The audio element correctly loads the track's local file URL from the catalog
Playback controls (play/pause/seek) respond correctly and the audio continues playing until stopped or track ends
No console errors related to audio loading or playback are present
The mini-player displays the currently playing track and updates its progress bar as the track plays

file_operations.description: Fix the audio playback implementation by ensuring the Audio element is properly instantiated, the play() promise is wrapped in try/catch to handle rejections, error event listeners are attached to catch loading failures, and state updates (isPlaying, currentTime, duration) are correctly synchronized with actual playback events. Add console logging for debugging audio loading and playback state transitions.

Verify that the play button onClick handler correctly invokes the audio player's play function with the track's file URL from the catalog. Ensure the active track highlighting works and that play/pause state is visually reflected. Add error boundary or error display if audio fails to load.

Ensure the mini-player component receives the currently playing track data and playback state from useAudioPlayer. Verify that progress bar updates are driven by currentTime/duration state changes. Add visual feedback if audio loading fails or playback encounters errors.

requirements.summary: Verify that all audio file URLs in the mood music catalog point to valid, accessible audio files in frontend/public directory
acceptanceCriteria: All track URLs in catalog.ts resolve to existing audio files
Audio files are in a supported format (mp3, ogg, or wav) that works across browsers
File paths are correctly formatted relative to the public directory
Loading any track URL in a browser plays the audio without 404 errors

file_operations.description: Review all track fileUrl entries to ensure they point to valid audio files in the frontend/public directory using correct relative paths (e.g., /assets/audio/trackname.mp3). Replace any missing or incorrect URLs with placeholder audio files or bundled sample tracks in supported formats (mp3, ogg, wav). Document the expected file structure in a comment at the top of the catalog.

Create the audio assets directory structure under frontend/public/assets/audio/ to hold local audio files referenced by the catalog. This ensures the directory exists and file paths resolve correctly. Add a .gitkeep file to preserve the directory in version control even if initially empty.

requirements.summary: Ensure the useAudioPlayer hook correctly instantiates and manages the HTML Audio element with proper error handling for loading failures
acceptanceCriteria: The Audio element is created and properly attached to the hook's state
Error events on the audio element are caught and logged or displayed to the user
The play() promise is handled correctly with try/catch to prevent unhandled rejections
State updates (isPlaying, currentTime, duration) reflect actual audio playback state

file_operations.description: Refactor useAudioPlayer to instantiate the Audio element in a useRef (not recreated on every render). Attach event listeners for 'loadedmetadata', 'timeupdate', 'ended', 'error', 'canplay', and 'pause' to synchronize state (duration, currentTime, isPlaying) with actual playback. Wrap audioElement.play() in try/catch to handle promise rejections (e.g., user interaction required). Add an error state to store and expose loading/playback errors to the UI. Log errors to the console for debugging.
